headline: In silico design of protein binders validated by structure prediction and docking
label: Computational Protein Binder Design
summary: Recent preprints pair generative design tools with structure-based scoring for binders against CRISPR, cartilage signaling, and autoimmune targets.
synthesis: The common thread is computational generation of protein-binding molecules followed by in silico assessment. The Cas9 study designs a VHH nanobody against the PI/RuvC interface of SpCas9 with BoltzGen and Boltz-2 and checks it with 10 ns molecular dynamics within a bivalent hub strategy. The BMPR1A study benchmarks RFdiffusion, BindCraft, PepMLM and RFpeptides across 290 designs, scored with AlphaFold 3 and physics-based metrics. The GluN1 study builds mimetic decoy peptides against anti-NMDAR autoantibodies using AlphaFold2, HADDOCK docking and PRODIGY scoring. What is distinct here is the emphasis on candidate generation and cross-tool ranking rather than conformational mechanism. The summaries describe computational outcomes only.
